notes: Vela v1.0 Pre-release (opt-in). This build makes HTTPS work on a device that has been running a while. The failure was never a shortage of free memory but of CONTIGUOUS memory: a handshake needs one unbroken ~16.9 KB block, and a non-moving collector cannot re-create a run that large once the heap is carved up. A measured Pico 2 W sat at 52 KB free with a largest block of 10 KB, and 'update check' failed every time. RPCortex now claims that block at boot, while the heap is still clean, and 'update check' on the same board succeeds. It is not a permanent tax: the block is handed back automatically once free memory gets tight, and taken again once there is room. Set Settings.TLS_Reserve to off to disable it. Also: update checks follow the channel of the build you are running and can no longer offer you an older version as an upgrade, and 'freeup' actually frees memory on a compiled image (measured 2 KB -> 84 KB). Pre-release — please report bugs.
features: HTTPS works after the device has been up a while: the contiguous block a TLS handshake needs is claimed at boot and given back automatically when memory gets tight
Update checks follow the channel of the build you are running, and a differing build id can no longer offer an older version as an upgrade
freeup actually frees memory on a compiled image — it evicts the command modules, not just the scope cache (measured 2 KB -> 84 KB on a Pico 2 W)
meminfo now reports the LARGEST ALLOCATABLE BLOCK and a fragmentation percentage, not just free memory — the GC never compacts, so free memory alone is misleading
New: defrag — reclaim and report whether there is enough contiguous RAM for HTTPS; defrag on|auto|off holds a block from boot (off by default)
New: safeboot [cmd] can STAGE an update to run on a serviceless maintenance boot (full RAM), then reboot back — reliable UI updates
Fixed: removing a package also removes its startup task + background service
Fixed: pkg install streams the archive to flash (512-byte chunks) — no more MemoryError on large packages; a partly-extracted package registers no command
DEVELOPER BUILD — the v0.9.5 multitasking foundation, now the default experience
Multitasking shell is the DEFAULT — background services keep running while you work (classic sync shell stays as the recovery / crash fallback)
Background services: httpd start --bg / status / stop; service list/add/remove/test
Cooperative app framework (appkit) — a foreground app (e.g. sysmon) yields so it runs alongside background services
Full async line editor — history, Tab completion, cursor + word navigation (shared LineEditor with the classic shell)
